sentences.text: Hualianceratops was a small, herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaur measuring approximately 1.2 meters in length.
Its skull was estimated to be 25 centimeters long.
In terms of overall size, this animal was comparable to a modern spaniel.
The lower jaw featured a deep and short dentary bone, while the upper jaw contained at least nine teeth.
The species Hualianceratops wucaiwanensis was formally named and described in 2015 by a team including Han Fenglu, Catherine A. Forster, James M. Clark, and Xu Xing.
The generic name combines Chinese words for 'ornamental face' with the Greek term for 'hornface' to highlight the decorative patterns on its jaw bones.
The holotype fossil, which serves as the primary specimen for the species, was discovered in the upper Shishugou Formation.
In 2015, researchers classified Hualianceratops within the family Chaoyangsauridae.
This dinosaur lived during the Oxfordian stage, a period spanning from 161.5 to 154.8 million years ago.
It inhabited western China during this time.
It remains unresolved how Hualianceratops relates to other members of its clade.
